title: Cascade - Postmortem & Escalation Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the March 3rd production incident: spike in tail latency after autoscale event caused by KV cache invalidation and a fallback to a quantized model that increased token generation time. Discussed mitigations (prefix caching, sticky routing to warm nodes, dedicated pilot), security artifacts requested, and concrete next steps for a Dedicated pilot and benchmark run.

transcript:
Meeting header - 2026-03-07 15:00 UTC; Duration: ~47m; Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Chen (Redwood CSM), Ari Thompson (Cascade VP Eng), Samira Patel (Cascade SRE), Leo Grant (Cascade Security), Nina Park (Cascade PM)

Summary: quick recap of prod incident on 2026-03-03 that caused elevated tail latency and intermittent 5xxs for a subset of requests. Goal: agree on root cause next steps and pilot scope for Dedicated nodes.

[00:00] Jordan: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight, we know this is high priority for you Ari so thanks for making time
[00:18] Ari: thanks, yeah we uh we got a bunch of engineers on standby, Samira's here my SRE, Leo from security, Nina from product, so we'll try to be concise
[00:35] Priya: quick agenda, we'll run through the timeline we reconstructed, show some early trace artifacts, talk through root cause hypotheses (KV cache invalidation + autoscale behavior + fallback to quantized variant), then mitigations and pilot proposal
[00:52] Samira: that sounds right, we've been digging in logs but the error spikes were kinda noisy around 03:10 UTC and then again around 03:37, we saw latencies jump from 200ms p95 to 3-5s for some requests
[01:12] Priya: yep our traces show a pattern where a node reaped in the autoscaler, KV cache lost some prefixes, subsequent requests had to regenerate large kv entries and that ended up hitting a fallback path where the routing layer selected the quantized model variant which has higher per-token decode costs in that codepath, plus concurrent regen caused blocking in the serving runtime, so tail spiked
[01:45] Ari: let me stop you — when you say fallback to a quantized model, like is that automatic? we didn't ask for quantized, our config pins the model to gpt-3.5-xx (example), is there a routing fallback?
[02:02] Jordan: good question — yeah by policy we have tiered variants, when the primary node is out of capacity or the model weights aren't warm, the smart router can pick a compatible variant to keep requests responding. In this incident the warm pool shrank and routing fell back to a quantized compat variant; typically that helps cost but in this case combined with regen it contributed to the latency spike
[02:28] Leo: from a security lens, did any of this touch PII or was it just transient internal state? we need to confirm audit logs and retention for the affected timeframe
[02:42] Marco: we'll include that in the artifact bundle, Jordan and I will pull request-level logs and the audit trail for the time window
[02:55] Samira: one thing we saw client-side — retried requests seemed to amplify load; clients did a 3x retry with exponential backoff but the backoff was too short and created a storm while cache was rebuilding
[03:17] Priya: yeah that's classic cascade effect, the combination of retries + cache regen + fallback path is the multiplier here
[03:30] Ari: okay, what's the root cause then? is it autoscaler config, routing logic, or something in the KV cache itself?
[03:40] Priya: our working hypothesis is mixed: primary trigger is an aggressive scale-down after a short idle window which killed warm nodes, that caused KV cache invalidation on some capacity, followed by workload with high prefix diversity which forced regenerations; the router then picked a quantized variant to preserve capacity; so it's a mix of autoscale policy + routing fallback behavior + workload shape
[04:05] Ari: can we reproduce this in staging? we need a deterministic repro to fix the root cause rather than bandaids
[04:12] Priya: yes we can, with a synthetic workload that has high prefix churn and short bursty windows; we proposed a Dedicated pilot where you pin capacity and avoid aggressive autoscale while we iterate — that will both reduce risk and let us run controlled benchmarks
[04:28] Nina: product question — what's the uplift or downside operationally if we go Dedicated? we care about cost and also about being able to failover to hosted if necessary
[04:38] Jordan: Dedicated gives you reserved warm nodes and predictable throughput; you can still configure fallback policies but the idea is to reduce autoscale churn. We can set up a canary route so some percentage of traffic goes to Dedicated during pilot then ramp. Cost is higher but it's predictable; we'll send pricing and a SOW
[04:56] Ari: good. Security: Leo, what do you need to sign off?
[05:02] Leo: audit logs, SOC2 artifact copies, SSO/SAML integration details, KMS key lifecycle docs, network topology for the Dedicated env (VPC peering or private link), and proof of encryption at rest for token caches - we need a written response for our InfoSec questionnaire
[05:22] Jordan: we can provide SOC2 report, architecture diagram for Dedicated with VPC peering notes, and KMS integration doc. We'll redact any customer PII but include audit log samples. We'll also provide RBAC/SSO setup guide
[05:36] Marco: I'll be owner on packaging the artifact set, we'll drop a link in the ticket and set permissions 
[05:45] Samira: operationally we want some short-term mitigations while pilot is set up: 1) increase autoscale cool-down to avoid rapid scale-downs, 2) temporarily disable the routing fallback to quantized variant for the affected route, 3) implement an aggressive prefix-level cache warming for next 72 hours
[06:05] Priya: agreed — we can push a config change to increase scale-down threshold and cool-down window; disabling fallback is doable per-route, though it reduces overall capacity headroom; warming can be done by synthetic background prefill jobs that run for a week
[06:25] Ari: risks with warming? does that increase cost meaningfully?
[06:30] Jordan: small cost for the prefill ops but far cheaper than customer impact from p95/p99 spikes. We'll include cost estimate in the SOW
[06:40] Nina: on the user side, we also want improved retry guidance in case of 5xx — we'd like a recommended backoff pattern from Redwood
[06:48] Priya: we can provide recommended client-side retry backoffs in the KB article and include it in the runbook
[06:55] Ari: ok good. can you give a quick timeline for the forensics and the pilot?
[07:02] Priya: immediate: Priya to run KV cache trace and produce a short artifact by 3/9; Jordan to send SOW and pricing by 3/8; Cascade to hand over sanitized sample traffic by 3/8; benchmark run target 3/10; pilot start target 3/15
[07:18] Samira: on logs, we need extended retention for the window, can you extend to 30 days for the support ticket?
[07:25] Marco: opened ticket SF-9982 and requested extended retention, we'll share link
[07:30] Leo: security follow ups — also need to confirm KMS integration won't store plaintext tokens in logs and confirm HSM usage if possible
[07:40] Jordan: yes we'll confirm KMS/HSM details; our default is envelope encryption and we do not log full plaintext tokens, only masked tokens; we'll include specifics in the artifact bundle
[07:55] Ari: anything else on root cause? do you think model quantization contributed more than autoscale?
[08:02] Priya: quantization exacerbated latency but the driver was cache regen + scale-down. The quantized variant has a slower decoding loop in that codepath we used for compat. We're doing a code change to avoid blocking regen paths and to make kv cache rebuilds async so they don't block request threads
[08:25] Ari: timeline for that change?
[08:28] Priya: small fix (non-blocking regen) is targeted for the next release train, EOD 3/20 for full rollout; short term we can avoid fallback and increase cool-down which should mitigate risk while we ship the change
[08:44] Nina: ok, let's document acceptance criteria for pilot: p95 < 500ms under our sample workload, no >1% 5xx over 24h, and RBAC+audit artifacts verified by InfoSec
[08:56] Jordan: noted — we'll include that in the SOW and bench spec
[09:02] Ari: good. security — Leo will validate artifacts within 48 hours of receiving them?
[09:09] Leo: yes, assuming we get them by 3/9 we can turn around by 3/11
[09:16] Marco: action items recap — I'll post a note in the ticket with owners and due dates and link to the shared doc (we'll attach the incident timeline, traces, and bench plan)
[09:28] Jordan: do we want a follow-up sync after artifacts are shared? propose 3/11 or 3/12 for a quick 30m check-in
[09:35] Ari: 3/11 1600 UTC works for us
[09:38] Jordan: great we'll send invite. Any other Qs?
[09:42] Samira: just one — can you confirm that the route change to disable fallback will not affect other teams using Redwood in our org? we have multiple product teams on different routes
[09:52] Priya: per-route config, we can restrict the change to the affected route only; we'll coordinate with your platform team to confirm route IDs
[10:02] Ari: ok thanks everyone.
